{"body":"## Summary
- harden OAuth response parsing, error sanitization, URL/resource validation, and STS subject token type configuration
- centralize OAuth HTTP error/origin helpers
- add mise-based lint/test tasks with govulncheck and update CI to use them
- refresh README security and embedding guidance

## Breaking changes to call out
- `tokenmanager` now defaults RFC 8693 `subject_token_type` to `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token` instead of `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt`; embedders whose STS requires the JWT URN should set `SubjectTokenType: sts.SubjectTokenTypeJWT`
- `tokenmanager.Token` now requires `TokenRequest.Resource` to be an origin URL; opaque/non-URL values should be sent via `Audience` rather than `Resource`

## Validation
- mise run lint
- mise run test:ci
- go vet ./...

---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes tighten OAuth HTTP parsing and token-exchange behavior (including new validation and default `subject_token_type`), which can break existing integrations and directly affect authentication/token handling. CI tooling changes are low risk, but the auth-path changes require careful review and testing against real providers.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Hardens OAuth client security checks and error handling across the library.** Centralizes OAuth response/error parsing in `internal/oauthhttp` (bounded reads with `ErrResponseTooLarge`, sanitized non-JSON fallbacks, and rejection of trailing JSON data), and updates `deviceflow`/`sts` to use these shared helpers.
> 
> **Tightens URL/origin rules and token-exchange defaults in `tokenmanager`.** `TokenRequest.Resource` is now validated as a strict origin URL (no path/query/fragment/userinfo; HTTPS unless loopback HTTP is explicitly enabled) and normalized before comparisons/cache keys, and `tokenmanager.Config` gains `SubjectTokenType` defaulting to RFC 8693 `access_token` URN (instead of `jwt`) for STS exchanges.
> 
> **Modernizes tooling/CI and docs.** Adds `mise` tasks (including `govulncheck`), updates GitHub Actions to run lint/tests via `mise`, bumps Go patch version, and refreshes `README`/`CHANGELOG` plus adds Entire hook/agent configuration files.

## Summary

Linear: [COR-174](https://linear.app/entire/issue/COR-174)

> [!NOTE]
> **STS endpoint will be moving soon.** v2 currently exposes the RFC 8693 token-exchange endpoint at `/api/authz/sts/token` (encoded in `provider.go`'s v2 surface). Server-side work is in flight to relocate it; once that lands, the new path moves into the auth-go repo's provider config in this CLI and the CLI side is a one-line bump.

Enables the partial.to staging deployment where the auth issuer (`us.auth.partial.to`) and the data API (`partial.to`) live on different origins by introducing per-resource RFC 8693 token exchange, then extracts the resulting library out of this repo into a standalone module so other internal CLIs can adopt the same pattern.

### Library: now lives at [github.com/entireio/auth-go](https://github.com/entireio/auth-go) (v0.1.0)

The `auth/` directory in this repo is gone — its contents have been split out via `git subtree split --prefix=auth` into a standalone MIT-licensed Go module with preserved history. The CLI now imports `github.com/entireio/auth-go/{deviceflow,sts,tokens,tokenstore,tokenmanager}` instead of carrying them inline.

What that buys us:
- **Shareable.** Other internal CLIs can `go get github.com/entireio/auth-go` and reuse the same OAuth plumbing instead of reimplementing it. No vendoring, no copy-paste drift.
- **No coupling.** The library has zero references to `github.com/entireio/cli` — every endpoint, identifier, and default value is supplied by `Config`.
- **Independent release cadence.** Tightening the library's public API doesn't gate on a CLI release; the CLI bumps when it wants to pick up new tags.

Subpackages, all provider-agnostic:
| Package | Role |
|---|---|
| `deviceflow` | RFC 8628 OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant client |
| `sts` | RFC 8693 OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange client |
| `tokens` | TokenSet value type + unverified JWT claim parsing (rejects `alg:none`) |
| `tokenstore` | Persistence interface + Keyring reference impl |
| `tokenmanager` | Orchestration: cache, JWT-aud shortcut, exchange dispatch |

### CLI-side wiring

- **Split-host config:** new `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` env var; `AuthBaseURL()` falls back to `BaseURL()` so single-host deployments are unchanged. Tokens are now keyed in the keyring by the auth issuer (the host that minted them). Auth-management commands (`auth list/revoke/status/logout`) routed to the auth host since their endpoints live there.
- **`NewAuthenticatedAPIClient` routes through the manager.** Data-API calls obtain a resource-audience bearer via RFC 8693 exchange when the core token's audience doesn't already match. All 8 callers thread `ctx`: activity, dispatch_wizard, recap, search, trail (×4 plus watch). Search additionally defaults `serviceURL` to `api.BaseURL()` and normalizes path-bearing URLs to scheme+host before token resolution.
- **Dispatch joins the manager-routed path.** `entire dispatch` was the last command sending the raw core token to the data API; mode_cloud now resolves through `auth.TokenForResource` like search/trail/recap.
- **v2 client_id aligned to `entire-cli`** (matched v1).
- **Provider table** carries `stsPath` per surface; v2's STS lives at `/api/authz/sts/token`. v1 is single-host, so its `stsPath` is empty and `tokenmanager.Config.STSPath` is optional — the same-host shortcut wins. Misconfigured split-host setups fail loudly via `ErrNoSTSPath`.

### Security hardening (defense in depth)

Four findings landed in addition to the core split-host work, all on top of server-side validation:

1. **Reject JWTs with `alg:none`** — `tokens.ParseClaims` decodes the JWT header and refuses the RFC 7515 unsigned shape. Case-insensitive, trims whitespace. Even though the CLI's claim use is documented as routing-only, the unsigned shape would let a hostile AS bypass shape checks. New `tokens.ErrUnsignedJWT` sentinel + 5 regression test cases.
2. **Enforce HTTPS on STS and device-flow endpoints.** Both clients reject `http://` BaseURLs unless `AllowInsecureHTTP` is set, which the CLI auto-permits only for loopback hosts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1). Production never qualifies; local dev does. New `ErrInsecureBaseURL` sentinel on each.
3. **Validate `verification_uri`** before showing it to the user or opening it in a browser. Rejects: non-URL, non-HTTPS (loopback http only), embedded userinfo (`user:pass@host` eye-trick), and control characters. New `ErrUnsafeVerificationURI` sentinel + comprehensive tests on safe/unsafe shapes.
4. **Validate received token in `login.go`** before persisting. `validateReceivedToken` parses the JWT (if it is one), rejects `alg:none`, hard-rejects `iss` mismatch vs. the configured issuer, and rejects already-expired `exp`. Opaque (non-JWT) tokens are permitted — the AS may not issue JWTs at all.

Plus a defense soph added earlier in PR #1156: the keyring fallback rejects JSON-shaped values so corruption never ships as a Bearer header.

### Other behaviour fixes surfaced during review

- `Store.LoadTokens` legacy bare-string fallback was unreachable — it only fired on `ErrNotFound`, but a pre-shim raw-token entry produced an unmarshal error. Added `tokenstore.ErrMalformed` so callers can distinguish "no entry" from "entry exists but malformed" and route the legacy path correctly.
- `tokenmanager.runExchange` was silently dropping `req.Resource` — `sts.ExchangeRequest.Resource` (RFC 8693 §2.1) was never sent to the AS.
- JWT-aud shortcut in `tokenmanager.Token` now gated on empty `Audience` so an explicit per-call `Audience` always forces an exchange (was silently downgraded if the core token's `aud` happened to include the resource).
- `tokenmanager.DeleteCoreToken` order swapped: keyring delete first, in-memory cache clear only on success — pre-emptive clear created a window where the CLI thought it was logged out but the keyring still held the token.
- `api.bearerTransport` rejects empty bearer at first request rather than putting `Authorization: Bearer<space>` on the wire (which produced confusing 401s).
- `PollDeviceAuth` shim now surfaces unknown OAuth error codes through `DeviceAuthPoll.Error` so login's polling loop fails fast on terminal rejections instead of retrying ~5×.
- `tokenmanager` cache key is now a struct map key instead of a delimiter-joined string — structurally collision-free.
- `freezeClock` in `deviceflow`/`sts` tests is no longer `t.Parallel()` (latent race against any future parallel test reading `nowFunc`).

### Test plan

- [x] `mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean.
- [x] `go test ./...` — only the two pre-existing main failures (`TestGroupCommitsByDay_SortsNewestFirst`, `TestExplainCmd_PositionalArgConflictsWithFlags`, plus `TestExplainCmd_SummaryTimeoutSecondsValidation` from a recent main commit) remain.
- [x] `go test -race ./...` — no new races.
- [x] `entireio/auth-go` repo builds and tests pass standalone at the v0.1.0 tag.
- [x] End-to-end against the partial.to staging deployment: `entire login`, `entire trail list`, `entire search`, `entire dispatch` all working through the device flow → STS exchange → resource-scoped bearer chain.

### Notes for reviewers

- The branch is 21 commits ahead of `main`. Easiest review path is by commit. The meaningful new work starts at `c492a54b1`. Most-substantial commits:
  - `c492a54b1` — split-host + tokenmanager (largest single change)
  - `a9aeb9e6f` — dispatch routing fix + the CLAUDE.md "Auth and token resolution" section + the auth-go README
  - `dc7c003e4` — soph's review follow-ups (PR #1156, already merged via merge commit)
  - `706a4a28e` — defense-in-depth security hardening (the four findings above)
  - `8821a55ae` — subtree extraction into [`entireio/auth-go`](https://github.com/entireio/auth-go); CLI imports rewritten, local `auth/` deleted
- The extracted-library PRs (constructor parity for `auth-go`'s `deviceflow.Client` / `sts.Client`, moving `tokenmanager.Config.Now`/`Exchange` off the public Config, renaming `TokenRequest.Resource` → `ResourceURL`, typed-error replacement of `descriptionFromSentinel`) now ship as `auth-go` v0.2.0 work, independent of this CLI PR.

questions.question: How would you like me to approach the auth-go integration on this branch?

options.label: Rebase PR #1153 onto soph/auth-go, then adapt for PR #5
options.description: Pull alex/cli-auth-consolidation's commits onto soph/auth-go, resolve conflicts with current main, then update for auth-go PR #5 breaking changes (Resource→origin URL, subject_token_type default). Preserves history & follow-up fixes.

options.label: Fresh implementation on soph/auth-go using PR #1153 as reference
options.description: Build the auth-go integration from scratch on this branch, using PR #1153's design as a guide but writing new commits. Cleaner history but more work and risk of missing edge cases PR #1153 already solved.

options.label: Smaller cut — just bump deps and patch breakage
options.description: Add github.com/entireio/auth-go as a dep, only migrate the minimum needed. Don't do the full split-host/STS exchange overhaul — leave that for PR #1153 to land separately.

questions.question: Which auth-go version should I target?

options.label: Latest released tag (v0.1.0) (Recommended)

options.label: PR #5 head (use replace directive or pseudo-version)
options.description: Pin to the unmerged PR #5 commit via go.mod replace/pseudo-version. Get the hardening now, but CI may break until PR #5 lands.

options.label: Wait for auth-go PR #5 to merge, then proceed

1	// Package tokenmanager orchestrates core-token storage and RFC 8693
2	// token exchanges for an OAuth 2.0 device-flow client.
3	//
4	// One Manager per CLI process. Construct it once from the embedding
5	// CLI's identity (Issuer, ClientID, STSPath, Store) and call
6	// TokenForResource / Token from data-API call sites.
7	//
8	// The package is provider-agnostic: every endpoint, identifier, and
9	// default value comes from Config. It has no env-var reads, no
10	// implicit URLs, and no embedded provider tables. Tests inject
11	// behaviour via SetExchangeForTest / SetNowForTest (see testseams.go)
12	// rather than via the public Config — keeping the STS call out of the
13	// caller-controllable surface.
14	package tokenmanager
15	
16	import (
17		"context"
18		"errors"
19		"fmt"
20		"net/http"
21		"net/url"
22		"strings"
23		"sync"
24		"sync/atomic"
25		"time"
26	
27		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/internal/oauthhttp"
28		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/sts"
29		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokens"
30		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokenstore"
31	)
32	
33	// DefaultRequestedTokenType is the RFC 8693 §3 URI used when neither
34	// Config.RequestedTokenType nor TokenRequest.RequestedTokenType is set.
35	// :access_token is the canonical "give me an OAuth access token" URI;
36	// the wire format is the server's choice.
37	//
38	//nolint:gosec // RFC 8693 token-type URI, not a credential
39	const DefaultRequestedTokenType = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token"
40	
41	// exchangeSkew is the safety margin applied when deciding whether a
42	// cached exchanged token is still usable. Set conservatively because
43	// the worst case (re-exchange one extra time per command) is cheap.
44	const exchangeSkew = 30 * time.Second
45	
46	// ErrNotLoggedIn is returned by Token / TokenForResource when no core
47	// token is present in the store. Callers can match on it to render a
48	// "run <login>" message.
49	var ErrNotLoggedIn = errors.New("not logged in")
50	
51	// ErrNoSTSPath is returned when an exchange is needed but Config.STSPath
52	// is empty. Single-host deployments hit the same-host shortcut and never
53	// reach this; split-host deployments must configure STSPath.
54	var ErrNoSTSPath = errors.New("token exchange required but Config.STSPath is empty")
55	
56	// Config configures a Manager.
57	type Config struct {
58		// Issuer is the auth host base URL where the device-flow login
59		// happened and STS exchanges are POSTed. Required. Doubles as the
60		// Store profile key, so a user can be logged into multiple issuers
61		// (e.g. regions / staging) without conflict.
62		Issuer string
63	
64		// ClientID identifies the public client per RFC 6749 §2.3.1 / §3.2.1.
65		// Sent on STS exchanges via the client_id form field. Required.
66		ClientID string
67	
68		// STSPath is the path on Issuer where token-exchange requests are
69		// POSTed. Optional: single-host deployments never trigger an
70		// exchange (the same-host shortcut wins) so they can leave it
71		// empty. When empty and an exchange is attempted, runExchange
72		// returns ErrNoSTSPath rather than POSTing to a bogus URL.
73		STSPath string
74	
75		// Store persists the core token. Required. Use any tokenstore.Store
76		// implementation; a per-CLI service name keeps credentials isolated
77		// from other CLIs sharing this library.
78		Store tokenstore.Store
79	
80		// RequestedTokenType is the default RFC 8693 requested_token_type
81		// URI. Empty → DefaultRequestedTokenType.
82		RequestedTokenType string
83	
84		// SubjectTokenType is the RFC 8693 subject_token_type sent on
85		// exchanges. Empty → sts.SubjectTokenTypeAccessToken, because the
86		// stored core token is an OAuth access token even when its wire format
87		// happens to be JWT.
88		SubjectTokenType string
89	
90		// Scope is the default scope sent on exchanges. Empty → omitted.
91		Scope string
92	
93		// UserAgent for HTTP requests. Empty → none.
94		UserAgent string
95	
96		// AllowInsecureHTTP permits exchanges against http:// issuers. Off
97		// by default — STS calls ship the user's core token in the request
98		// body and must be TLS-protected. Only flip this for local/dev
99		// deployments pinned to loopback.
100		AllowInsecureHTTP bool
101	
102		// Transport overrides the http.RoundTripper used for STS calls.
103		// Useful for installing a debug logger or proxy. nil →
104		// http.DefaultTransport. Replaces the previous HTTPClient field —
105		// see sts.Client.Transport for the security rationale.
106		Transport http.RoundTripper
107	}
108	
109	func (c Config) validate() error {
110		switch {
111		case strings.TrimSpace(c.Issuer) == "":
112			return errors.New("Config.Issuer is required")
113		case strings.TrimSpace(c.ClientID) == "":
114			return errors.New("Config.ClientID is required")
115		case c.Store == nil:
116			return errors.New("Config.Store is required")
117		}
118		return nil
119	}
120	
121	// exchangeFunc / nowFuncType are named so we can hold them in
122	// atomic.Pointer values. Storing the override behind an
123	// atomic.Pointer rather than a plain field plus mu lets the hot read
124	// paths (runExchange, m.now) avoid taking the lock — they were
125	// previously racing with SetExchangeForTest / SetNowForTest.
126	type exchangeFunc func(ctx context.Context, req sts.ExchangeRequest) (*tokens.TokenSet, error)
127	type nowFuncType func() time.Time
128	
129	// Manager orchestrates core-token storage and STS exchanges. Safe for
130	// concurrent use.
131	type Manager struct {
132		cfg Config
133	
134		mu    sync.Mutex
135		cache map[cacheKey]cachedToken
136	
137		// Test seams. Set only via SetExchangeForTest / SetNowForTest,
138		// both of which require a testing.TB to discourage production
139		// callers from synthesising a fake TB to bypass STS. Held behind
140		// atomic.Pointer so hot-path reads (runExchange, now) don't race
141		// against test setup/teardown.
142		exchangeOverride atomic.Pointer[exchangeFunc]
143		nowOverride      atomic.Pointer[nowFuncType]
144	}
145	
146	// now returns the manager's effective clock. Tests can replace it via
147	// SetNowForTest; production callers always get time.Now.
148	func (m *Manager) now() time.Time {
149		if p := m.nowOverride.Load(); p != nil {
150			return (*p)()
151		}
152		return time.Now()
153	}
154	
155	// New builds a Manager from cfg. Returns an error when required
156	// fields are missing or Issuer is not an absolute URL.
157	//
158	// Issuer is normalized via RFC 3986 §6.2.2 (lowercase scheme/host,
159	// default-port stripped, no trailing slash) before being used as the
160	// Store profile key and as the same-host shortcut comparison. Without
161	// this, two Managers configured with cosmetically-different issuers
162	// (`https://auth.example.com/` vs `https://auth.example.com`) would
163	// write to different keyring entries but compare equal for the
164	// shortcut — one Manager handing out the other's tokens.
165	func New(cfg Config) (*Manager, error) {
166		if err := cfg.validate(); err != nil {
167			return nil, err
168		}
169		parsed, err := url.Parse(cfg.Issuer)
170		if err != nil || parsed.Scheme == "" || parsed.Host == "" {
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("Config.Issuer must be an absolute URL with scheme and host, got %q", cfg.Issuer)
172		}
173		cfg.Issuer = oauthhttp.NormalizeOriginURL(cfg.Issuer)
174		if cfg.RequestedTokenType == "" {
175			cfg.RequestedTokenType = DefaultRequestedTokenType
176		}
177		if cfg.SubjectTokenType == "" {
178			cfg.SubjectTokenType = sts.SubjectTokenTypeAccessToken
179		}
180		return &Manager{cfg: cfg, cache: map[cacheKey]cachedToken{}}, nil
181	}
182	
183	// Issuer returns the configured issuer URL.
184	func (m *Manager) Issuer() string { return m.cfg.Issuer }
185	
186	// SaveCoreToken persists the device-flow access token under the
187	// configured Issuer.
188	//
189	// On successful save the in-memory exchange cache is cleared so a
190	// re-login under a different identity can't return the previous user's
191	// exchanged tokens. The cacheKey already binds entries to CoreToken so
192	// this is defence-in-depth against a future refactor that drops the
193	// core token from the cache key — see TestSaveCoreToken_ClearsExchangeCache.
194	func (m *Manager) SaveCoreToken(accessToken string) error {
195		if err := m.cfg.Store.SaveTokens(m.cfg.Issuer, tokens.TokenSet{AccessToken: accessToken}); err != nil {
196			return fmt.Errorf("save core token: %w", err)
197		}
198		m.mu.Lock()
199		m.cache = map[cacheKey]cachedToken{}
200		m.mu.Unlock()
201		return nil
202	}
203	
204	// LookupCoreToken returns the stored core token, or "" if none is
205	// stored. A nil-return-no-error mirrors how callers expect
206	// "not-logged-in" to look.
207	func (m *Manager) LookupCoreToken() (string, error) {
208		t, err := m.cfg.Store.LoadTokens(m.cfg.Issuer)
209		if errors.Is(err, tokenstore.ErrNotFound) {
210			return "", nil
211		}
212		if err != nil {
213			return "", fmt.Errorf("load core token: %w", err)
214		}
215		return t.AccessToken, nil
216	}
217	
218	// DeleteCoreToken removes the stored core token and any cached
219	// exchanges derived from it.
220	//
221	// Order matters: the keyring delete runs first, then the in-memory
222	// cache is cleared. If the keyring delete fails the cache is left
223	// alone — clearing it pre-emptively would create a window where the
224	// CLI thinks it's logged out (no cache entries) but the keyring
225	// still hands out the core token to the next process.
226	func (m *Manager) DeleteCoreToken() error {
227		if err := m.cfg.Store.DeleteTokens(m.cfg.Issuer); err != nil {
228			return fmt.Errorf("delete core token: %w", err)
229		}
230		m.mu.Lock()
231		m.cache = map[cacheKey]cachedToken{}
232		m.mu.Unlock()
233		return nil
234	}
235	
236	// TokenRequest customises one Token call. Empty fields fall back to
237	// Config defaults.
238	type TokenRequest struct {
239		// Resource is the origin where the bearer will be presented.
240		// Required. Used for the same-host shortcut, the JWT-aud shortcut,
241		// and as part of the cache key.
242		Resource string
243	
244		// Audience is the wire-level RFC 8693 audience parameter. Empty →
245		// omitted (the AS picks). Independent of Resource — most callers
246		// leave Audience empty.
247		Audience string
248	
249		// RequestedTokenType overrides Config.RequestedTokenType for this
250		// call. Empty → Config default.
251		RequestedTokenType string
252	
253		// Scope overrides Config.Scope for this call. Empty → Config default.
254		Scope string
255	}
256	
257	// TokenForResource is a convenience for Token using only Resource.
258	func (m *Manager) TokenForResource(ctx context.Context, resourceBaseURL string) (string, error) {
259		return m.Token(ctx, TokenRequest{Resource: resourceBaseURL})
260	}
261	
262	// Token resolves a bearer token for use against req.Resource,
263	// performing an RFC 8693 exchange when needed.
264	//
265	// Resolution rules:
266	//
267	//  1. No core token in the store → ErrNotLoggedIn.
268	//  2. m.Issuer() == req.Resource (and req.Audience is empty) → use
269	//     the core token directly. Single-host deployments hit this path.
270	//  3. Core token's `aud` claim already includes req.Resource → use
271	//     the core token directly. Multi-audience tokens skip exchange.
272	//  4. Otherwise → RFC 8693 token exchange.
273	//
274	// Successful exchanges are cached in-memory keyed by (core token,
275	// resource, audience, requested-token-type, scope) until expiry.
276	func (m *Manager) Token(ctx context.Context, req TokenRequest) (string, error) {
277		if strings.TrimSpace(req.Resource) == "" {
278			return "", errors.New("TokenRequest.Resource is required")
279		}
280		normResource, err := oauthhttp.ValidateOriginURL(req.Resource, m.cfg.AllowInsecureHTTP, "TokenRequest.Resource")
281		if err != nil {
282			return "", err
283		}
284	
285		core, err := m.LookupCoreToken()
286		if err != nil {
287			return "", err
288		}
289		if core == "" {
290			return "", ErrNotLoggedIn
291		}
292		// Preflight expiry: a long-stored core token would otherwise hit the
293		// resource (or STS) and surface as a confusing "invalid_grant" /
294		// "401". Parse-failure is intentionally not treated as expired —
295		// opaque (non-JWT) access tokens have no client-visible expiry, so
296		// we let them flow and trust the server to reject if necessary.
297		if coreTokenExpired(core, m.now()) {
298			return "", ErrNotLoggedIn
299		}
300	
301		// m.cfg.Issuer was normalized at New() time, so no re-normalize here.
302		if req.Audience == "" && m.cfg.Issuer == normResource {
303			return core, nil
304		}
305		if req.Audience == "" && coreTokenAudienceIncludes(core, normResource) {
306			return core, nil
307		}
308	
309		resolved := m.resolve(req)
310		resolved.Resource = normResource
311		key := makeCacheKey(core, resolved, normResource)
312		if hit, ok := m.cacheLookup(key); ok {
313			return hit, nil
314		}
315	
316		exchanged, err := m.runExchange(ctx, core, resolved)
317		if err != nil {
318			return "", err
319		}
320		m.cacheStore(key, exchanged)
321		return exchanged.AccessToken, nil
322	}
323	
324	// resolve fills empty TokenRequest fields with Config defaults.
325	func (m *Manager) resolve(req TokenRequest) TokenRequest {
326		if req.RequestedTokenType == "" {
327			req.RequestedTokenType = m.cfg.RequestedTokenType
328		}
329		if req.Scope == "" {
330			req.Scope = m.cfg.Scope
331		}
332		return req
333	}
334	
335	// coreTokenExpired reports whether the core token has an `exp` claim
336	// in the past at now. JWT parse failures (and tokens without an `exp`
337	// claim) are reported as not-expired so opaque access tokens flow
338	// through the rest of the resolution rules unchanged.
339	func coreTokenExpired(coreJWT string, now time.Time) bool {
340		claims, err := tokens.ParseClaims(coreJWT)
341		if err != nil {
342			return false
343		}
344		if claims.ExpiresAt.IsZero() {
345			return false
346		}
347		return !now.Before(claims.ExpiresAt)
348	}
349	
350	// coreTokenAudienceIncludes reports whether the core JWT's `aud` claim
351	// covers target. target is expected to already be in normalised form;
352	// aud entries are normalised here so a trailing-slash / case difference
353	// between the AS and the caller doesn't force a needless STS exchange.
354	func coreTokenAudienceIncludes(coreJWT, target string) bool {
355		claims, err := tokens.ParseClaims(coreJWT)
356		if err != nil {
357			return false
358		}
359		for _, aud := range claims.Audience {
360			if oauthhttp.NormalizeOriginURL(aud) == target {
361				return true
362			}
363		}
364		return false
365	}
366	
367	// maxCachedTokenLifetime bounds entries with an unknown wire-side
368	// expiry. Today this can't happen on the exchange path (sts.Exchange
369	// rejects non-positive expires_in), but it would still apply if a
370	// future code path stored a TokenSet without ExpiresAt — capping at 1h
371	// prevents an indefinitely-cached stale token in that case.
372	const maxCachedTokenLifetime = time.Hour
373	
374	// cachedToken is one entry in the per-process exchange cache.
375	type cachedToken struct {
376		accessToken string
377		expiresAt   time.Time
378		cachedAt    time.Time
379	}
380	
381	func (c cachedToken) usable(now time.Time) bool {
382		if c.accessToken == "" {
383			return false
384		}
385		if c.expiresAt.IsZero() {
386			return now.Sub(c.cachedAt) < maxCachedTokenLifetime
387		}
388		return now.Add(exchangeSkew).Before(c.expiresAt)
389	}
390	
391	// cacheKey is a structurally-keyed exchange-cache key. Using a struct
392	// rather than a delimiter-joined string sidesteps any chance of two
393	// distinct (core token, resource, audience, requested-token-type,
394	// scope) tuples hashing to the same map slot via embedded delimiters
395	// in any field.
396	type cacheKey struct {
397		CoreToken          string
398		Resource           string
399		Audience           string
400		RequestedTokenType string
401		Scope              string
402	}
403	
404	// makeCacheKey builds a cacheKey from the (resolved) request. Includes
405	// every wire-affecting field so different combinations don't shadow
406	// each other. normalizedResource is the caller-supplied Resource after
407	// normalisation, so https://api.example.com and
408	// https://api.example.com/ share a single cache entry.
409	func makeCacheKey(coreToken string, req TokenRequest, normalizedResource string) cacheKey {
410		return cacheKey{
411			CoreToken:          coreToken,
412			Resource:           normalizedResource,
413			Audience:           req.Audience,
414			RequestedTokenType: req.RequestedTokenType,
415			Scope:              req.Scope,
416		}
417	}
418	
419	func (m *Manager) cacheLookup(key cacheKey) (string, bool) {
420		m.mu.Lock()
421		defer m.mu.Unlock()
422		entry, ok := m.cache[key]
423		if !ok {
424			return "", false
425		}
426		if !entry.usable(m.now()) {
427			delete(m.cache, key)
428			return "", false
429		}
430		return entry.accessToken, true
431	}
432	
433	func (m *Manager) cacheStore(key cacheKey, t *tokens.TokenSet) {
434		m.mu.Lock()
435		defer m.mu.Unlock()
436		m.cache[key] = cachedToken{
437			accessToken: t.AccessToken,
438			expiresAt:   t.ExpiresAt,
439			cachedAt:    m.now(),
440		}
441	}
442	
443	// runExchange dispatches to either Config.Exchange (test override) or
444	// a freshly built sts.Client pointing at m.cfg.Issuer + m.cfg.STSPath.
445	func (m *Manager) runExchange(ctx context.Context, coreToken string, req TokenRequest) (*tokens.TokenSet, error) {
446		stsReq := sts.ExchangeRequest{
447			SubjectToken:       coreToken,
448			SubjectTokenType:   m.cfg.SubjectTokenType,
449			RequestedTokenType: req.RequestedTokenType,
450			Audience:           req.Audience,
451			Resource:           req.Resource,
452			Scope:              req.Scope,
453			// Public-client identification per RFC 6749 §2.3.1 / §3.2.1.
454			// Carried via Extra because the sts package is provider-agnostic.
455			Extra: url.Values{"client_id": {m.cfg.ClientID}},
456		}
457	
458		if p := m.exchangeOverride.Load(); p != nil {
459			return (*p)(ctx, stsReq)
460		}
461	
462		if strings.TrimSpace(m.cfg.STSPath) == "" {
463			return nil, ErrNoSTSPath
464		}
465	
466		stsClient := &sts.Client{
467			Transport:         m.cfg.Transport,
468			BaseURL:           m.cfg.Issuer,
469			Path:              m.cfg.STSPath,
470			UserAgent:         m.cfg.UserAgent,
471			AllowInsecureHTTP: m.cfg.AllowInsecureHTTP,
472		}
473		return stsClient.Exchange(ctx, stsReq) //nolint:wrapcheck // sts.Exchange already prefixes "token exchange:"
474	}

2	// Grant client.
3	//
4	// Construct a Client with the issuer's BaseURL plus the paths and
5	// client_id it expects, then call StartDeviceAuth followed by repeated
6	// PollDeviceAuth calls until either a TokenSet comes back or a
7	// terminal error is returned. Caller drives the polling loop and
8	// adjusts the interval on ErrSlowDown per RFC 8628 §3.5.
9	//
10	// The client is provider-agnostic: every server-specific value
11	// (endpoint paths, client_id, optional scope) is configured at
12	// construction time. There is no provider detection.
13	package deviceflow
14	
15	import (
16		"context"
17		"errors"
18		"fmt"
19		"net/http"
20		"net/url"
21		"strings"

25		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokens"
26	)

28	// nowFunc is the package's clock. Tests override it; production uses
29	// time.Now.
30	var nowFunc = time.Now
31	
32	// deviceCodeGrantType is the RFC 8628 token-endpoint grant_type for
33	// polling device-flow authorization.
34	const deviceCodeGrantType = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code"
35	
36	// DeviceCode is the response from the device authorization endpoint
37	// (RFC 8628 §3.2). Pass DeviceCode through to subsequent PollDeviceAuth
38	// calls and show UserCode + VerificationURI to the user.
39	type DeviceCode struct {
40		DeviceCode              string `json:"device_code"`
41		UserCode                string `json:"user_code"`
42		VerificationURI         string `json:"verification_uri"`
43		VerificationURIComplete string `json:"verification_uri_complete"`
44		ExpiresIn               int    `json:"expires_in"`
45		Interval                int    `json:"interval"`
46	}
47	
48	// DefaultRequestTimeout caps a single device-flow HTTP round-trip
49	// (StartDeviceAuth or one PollDeviceAuth call). Set conservatively:
50	// healthy device-flow endpoints respond in sub-seconds, so the cap
51	// mainly defends against slow-loris responses dripping bytes within
52	// MaxResponseBytes — see Client.RequestTimeout for the per-Client
53	// override. The polling-loop interval is the caller's concern; this
54	// timeout governs only the individual HTTP request.
55	const DefaultRequestTimeout = 30 * time.Second
56	
57	// Client polls an RFC 8628 device authorization grant.
58	//
59	// All configuration is explicit; the package has no global state and
60	// no implicit URLs. Provide BaseURL, ClientID, and the two endpoint
61	// paths; the rest is RFC 8628 mechanics.
62	type Client struct {
63		// Transport supplies the http.RoundTripper used for all calls.
64		// nil → http.DefaultTransport. The library builds its own
65		// *http.Client around this transport so callers can't trivially
66		// pass a *http.Client with a misconfigured TLS bypass (the prior
67		// HTTP *http.Client field made that a one-liner). Custom
68		// RoundTrippers that wrap or replace TLS verification remain the
69		// caller's responsibility; this hook is for observability
70		// (request/response logging) and per-environment proxies, not
71		// security bypass.
72		Transport http.RoundTripper
73	
74		BaseURL        string
75		ClientID       string
76		Scope          string
77		UserAgent      string
78		DeviceCodePath string
79		TokenPath      string
80	
81		// RequestTimeout is the per-request deadline applied via
82		// context.WithTimeout on top of the caller's context. Zero falls
83		// back to DefaultRequestTimeout. Negative disables the cap (useful
84		// for tests that want to drive timing via the caller's ctx alone).
85		RequestTimeout time.Duration
86	
87		// AllowInsecureHTTP permits http:// BaseURLs. Default (false) is
88		// reject — the device-flow token endpoint returns the user's
89		// freshly-minted access token in the response body and must be
90		// TLS-protected end to end. Production callers MUST leave this
91		// false; only tests and local development pinned to loopback
92		// should flip it.
93		AllowInsecureHTTP bool
94	}
95	
96	// httpClient builds the *http.Client used for one request. See
97	// oauthhttp.HTTPClient for the construction policy (fresh per call,
98	// shared underlying Transport, no Client.Timeout).
99	func (c *Client) httpClient() *http.Client {
100		return oauthhttp.HTTPClient(c.Transport)
101	}
102	
103	// requestTimeout resolves the effective per-request timeout: the
104	// configured RequestTimeout if positive, the package default if zero,
105	// or zero (no cap) if negative.
106	func (c *Client) requestTimeout() time.Duration {
107		switch {
108		case c.RequestTimeout < 0:
109			return 0
110		case c.RequestTimeout == 0:
111			return DefaultRequestTimeout
112		default:
113			return c.RequestTimeout
114		}
115	}
116	
117	// Sentinel errors returned by PollDeviceAuth when the token endpoint
118	// responds with a recognised RFC 8628 §3.5 error code. Callers branch
119	// on these with errors.Is and adjust their polling loop accordingly.
120	var (
121		// ErrAuthorizationPending — user has not yet approved or denied.
122		// Caller polls again at the existing interval.
123		ErrAuthorizationPending = errors.New("authorization_pending")
124	
125		// ErrSlowDown — caller is polling too fast. Caller bumps the
126		// interval (per RFC 8628 §3.5, by at least 5 seconds) and tries
127		// again.
128		ErrSlowDown = errors.New("slow_down")
129	
130		// ErrAccessDenied — user denied the request. Terminal.
131		ErrAccessDenied = errors.New("access_denied")
132	
133		// ErrExpiredToken — device code expired before the user approved.
134		// Terminal; restart with a fresh StartDeviceAuth.
135		ErrExpiredToken = errors.New("expired_token")
136	
137		// ErrInvalidGrant — device code already redeemed, malformed, or
138		// otherwise rejected. Terminal.
139		ErrInvalidGrant = errors.New("invalid_grant")
140	)
141	
142	// errCodeToSentinel maps an RFC 8628 §3.5 error code string to the
143	// matching sentinel. Unknown codes fall through to a generic error.
144	func errCodeToSentinel(code string) error {
145		switch code {
146		case "authorization_pending":
147			return ErrAuthorizationPending
148		case "slow_down":
149			return ErrSlowDown
150		case "access_denied":
151			return ErrAccessDenied
152		case "expired_token":
153			return ErrExpiredToken
154		case "invalid_grant":
155			return ErrInvalidGrant
156		default:
157			return fmt.Errorf("oauth error: %s", code)
158		}
159	}
160	
161	// StartDeviceAuth requests a fresh device code from the authorization
162	// server. The returned DeviceCode is opaque to the client; pass it
163	// back unmodified on every PollDeviceAuth.
164	func (c *Client) StartDeviceAuth(ctx context.Context) (*DeviceCode, error) {
165		if timeout := c.requestTimeout(); timeout > 0 {
166			var cancel context.CancelFunc
167			ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
168			defer cancel()
169		}
170	
171		body := url.Values{}
172		body.Set("client_id", c.ClientID)
173		if c.Scope != "" {
174			body.Set("scope", c.Scope)
175		}
176	
177		resp, err := c.postForm(ctx, c.DeviceCodePath, body)
178		if err != nil {
179			return nil, fmt.Errorf("start device auth: %w", err)
180		}
181		defer resp.Body.Close()
182	
183		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
184			return nil, readAPIError(resp, "start device auth")
185		}
186	
187		var result DeviceCode
188		if err := oauthhttp.ReadAndDecodeJSON(resp.Body, &result, true); err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("start device auth: %w", err)
190		}
191		if err := validateVerificationURI(result.VerificationURI, c.AllowInsecureHTTP); err != nil {
192			return nil, fmt.Errorf("start device auth: verification_uri: %w", err)
193		}
194		if result.VerificationURIComplete != "" {
195			if err := validateVerificationURI(result.VerificationURIComplete, c.AllowInsecureHTTP); err != nil {
196				return nil, fmt.Errorf("start device auth: verification_uri_complete: %w", err)
197			}
198		}
199		return &result, nil
200	}
201	
202	// ErrUnsafeVerificationURI is returned when the authorization server
203	// returns a verification_uri that fails minimum-trust checks. Defense
204	// against a compromised or misconfigured AS pointing users at a
205	// phishing page: the URL we'd otherwise echo to the user and open in
206	// their browser carries the user code, so a wrong destination is a
207	// direct credential-harvesting vector.
208	var ErrUnsafeVerificationURI = errors.New("unsafe verification_uri")
209	
210	// validateVerificationURI rejects URIs that obviously look like
211	// phishing or shell-injection attempts:
212	//
213	//   - Must parse as an absolute URL.
214	//   - Scheme must be https (or http only when allowInsecureHTTP is
215	//     set AND the host is loopback — production never qualifies).
216	//   - Must not embed userinfo (user:password@host tricks the eye).
217	//   - Must not contain control characters (CR/LF/etc.) that could
218	//     break terminal output or sneak past glance-checks.
219	//
220	// This is the bottom-floor check; the embedding CLI is still expected
221	// to show the URL to the user for visual inspection, and the user is
222	// expected to read it before opening.
223	func validateVerificationURI(raw string, allowInsecureHTTP bool) error {
224		if raw == "" {
225			return fmt.Errorf("%w: missing", ErrUnsafeVerificationURI)
226		}
227		for _, r := range raw {
228			if r < 0x20 || r == 0x7f {
229				return fmt.Errorf("%w: contains control character", ErrUnsafeVerificationURI)
230			}
231		}
232		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
233		if err != nil {
234			return fmt.Errorf("%w: parse: %w", ErrUnsafeVerificationURI, err)
235		}
236		if u.Host == "" {
237			return fmt.Errorf("%w: missing host", ErrUnsafeVerificationURI)
238		}
239		if u.User != nil {
240			return fmt.Errorf("%w: embedded userinfo not permitted", ErrUnsafeVerificationURI)
241		}
242		switch u.Scheme {
243		case "https":
244			// fine
245		case "http":

248			}

250				return fmt.Errorf("%w: http only permitted on loopback hosts", ErrUnsafeVerificationURI)
251			}

253			return fmt.Errorf("%w: scheme %q (must be https)", ErrUnsafeVerificationURI, u.Scheme)
254		}
255		return nil
256	}
257	
258	// PollDeviceAuth exchanges deviceCode for a TokenSet at the token
259	// endpoint.
260	//
261	// On success, returns a TokenSet with absolute expiry derived from
262	// the server's expires_in. On any RFC 8628 §3.5 error code, returns
263	// the matching sentinel error from this package. Other failures
264	// (network, malformed responses) are wrapped with context.
265	//
266	// Most callers want PollUntil instead — it drives the poll loop,
267	// honours the interval, applies the RFC 8628 §3.5 +5s slow_down bump,
268	// and stops at the device-code's ExpiresIn ceiling. Use PollDeviceAuth
269	// directly only when you need to render the per-tick state yourself
270	// (e.g. animating a TUI spinner).
271	func (c *Client) PollDeviceAuth(ctx context.Context, deviceCode string) (*tokens.TokenSet, error) {
272		if timeout := c.requestTimeout(); timeout > 0 {
273			var cancel context.CancelFunc
274			ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
275			defer cancel()
276		}
277	
278		body := url.Values{}
279		body.Set("grant_type", deviceCodeGrantType)
280		body.Set("client_id", c.ClientID)
281		body.Set("device_code", deviceCode)
282	
283		resp, err := c.postForm(ctx, c.TokenPath, body)
284		if err != nil {
285			return nil, fmt.Errorf("poll device auth: %w", err)
286		}
287		defer resp.Body.Close()
288	
289		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
290			return nil, readAPIError(resp, "poll device auth")
291		}
292	
293		var raw struct {
294			AccessToken  string `json:"access_token"`
295			TokenType    string `json:"token_type"`
296			ExpiresIn    int    `json:"expires_in"`
297			RefreshToken string `json:"refresh_token"`
298			Scope        string `json:"scope"`
299		}
300		if err := oauthhttp.ReadAndDecodeJSON(resp.Body, &raw, false); err != nil {
301			return nil, fmt.Errorf("poll device auth: %w", err)
302		}
303	
304		if raw.AccessToken == "" {
305			return nil, errors.New("poll device auth: server returned 200 with no access token")
306		}
307	
308		t := &tokens.TokenSet{
309			AccessToken:  raw.AccessToken,
310			RefreshToken: raw.RefreshToken,
311			TokenType:    raw.TokenType,
312			Scope:        raw.Scope,
313		}
314		if raw.ExpiresIn > 0 {
315			t.ExpiresAt = nowFunc().Add(time.Duration(raw.ExpiresIn) * time.Second)
316		}
317		return t, nil
318	}
319	
320	// postForm POSTs body as application/x-www-form-urlencoded to a path
321	// resolved against the client's BaseURL. The caller is responsible
322	// for applying any per-request timeout via context.WithTimeout — the
323	// timeout must cover the body-read that happens after postForm
324	// returns, so cancel-on-return here would interrupt that read.
325	func (c *Client) postForm(ctx context.Context, path string, body url.Values) (*http.Response, error) {
326		endpoint, err := resolveURL(c.BaseURL, path, c.AllowInsecureHTTP)
327		if err != nil {
328			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve URL %s: %w", path, err)
329		}
330	
331		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, endpoint, strings.NewReader(body.Encode()))
332		if err != nil {
333			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create request: %w", err)
334		}
335	
336		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
337		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
338		if c.UserAgent != "" {
339			req.Header.Set("User-Agent", c.UserAgent)
340		}
341	
342		resp, err := c.httpClient().Do(req)
343		if err != nil {
344			return nil, fmt.Errorf("request %s: %w", path, err)
345		}
346		return resp, nil
347	}
348	
349	// ErrInsecureBaseURL is returned when device-flow requests are made
350	// against an http:// BaseURL without AllowInsecureHTTP set. The token
351	// endpoint returns the user's access token in the response body — over
352	// plain HTTP that's a credential in the clear. Re-exported from
353	// internal/oauthhttp so callers can errors.Is(err, deviceflow.ErrInsecureBaseURL)
354	// regardless of which package raised it.
355	var ErrInsecureBaseURL = oauthhttp.ErrInsecureBaseURL
356	
357	// ErrAbsolutePath is returned when DeviceCodePath or TokenPath is an
358	// absolute or scheme-relative URL rather than a path relative to
359	// BaseURL. Go's url.ResolveReference *replaces* the base when handed
360	// an absolute reference, so accepting an absolute path would let any
361	// caller who can influence the configuration (env var, config file,
362	// server-discovery doc) redirect the device-code or token request to
363	// an attacker — and in the token-endpoint case, capture the user's
364	// access token. Re-exported from internal/oauthhttp.
365	var ErrAbsolutePath = oauthhttp.ErrAbsolutePath
366	
367	func resolveURL(baseURL, path string, allowInsecureHTTP bool) (string, error) {
368		return oauthhttp.ResolveURL(baseURL, path, allowInsecureHTTP) //nolint:wrapcheck // pass through with sentinel-preserving semantics
369	}
370	
371	// readAPIError surfaces an error-shaped response. It routes the AS's
372	// `error` code through errCodeToSentinel so callers can errors.Is
373	// regardless of which endpoint produced the failure, and appends a
374	// sanitised error_description when one was supplied — capping length
375	// and stripping control characters that would otherwise let a hostile
376	// AS write ANSI escapes / overflow into the user's terminal.
377	func readAPIError(resp *http.Response, action string) error {
378		apiErr, parseErr := oauthhttp.ReadOAuthError(resp)
379		if parseErr != nil {
380			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", action, parseErr)
381		}
382		err := errCodeToSentinel(apiErr.Error)
383		if desc := sanitizeDescription(apiErr.ErrorDescription); desc != "" {
384			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w: %s", action, err, desc)
385		}
386		return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", action, err)
387	}
388	
389	// sanitizeDescription is a thin alias kept for in-package readability.
390	// The implementation lives in internal/oauthhttp.
391	func sanitizeDescription(s string) string { return oauthhttp.SanitizeDescription(s) }
392	
393	// slowDownBump is the per-RFC 8628 §3.5 mandated interval increase
394	// applied each time the AS responds with `slow_down`. RFC says "at
395	// least 5 seconds"; we go with exactly 5. Declared as a var rather
396	// than const so PollUntil tests can shrink it without burning real
397	// wall-clock seconds. Production callers should never mutate this.
398	var slowDownBump = 5 * time.Second
399	
400	// pollInterval picks the effective poll interval for a device-code
401	// response.
402	//
403	//   - RFC 8628 §3.5 lets the AS omit `interval`, in which case the
404	//     client SHOULD use 5 seconds.
405	//   - Non-positive values (omitted, zero, negative) fall back to
406	//     defaultInterval — a literal `"interval":0` would otherwise hot-
407	//     loop against the token endpoint.
408	//   - Values past maxIntervalSeconds are clamped to 1h. Without a
409	//     ceiling, a hostile or buggy AS could effectively park the poll
410	//     loop until ExpiresIn fires; on 64-bit platforms an extreme
411	//     value could also overflow time.Duration's nanosecond range
412	//     (max ~292y). 1h is several orders of magnitude above any real
413	//     device-flow interval and still safely bounded.
414	func pollInterval(dc *DeviceCode) time.Duration {
415		const defaultInterval = 5 * time.Second
416		const maxIntervalSeconds = 3600
417		switch {
418		case dc.Interval <= 0:
419			return defaultInterval
420		case dc.Interval > maxIntervalSeconds:
421			return time.Duration(maxIntervalSeconds) * time.Second
422		default:
423			return time.Duration(dc.Interval) * time.Second
424		}
425	}
426	
427	// PollUntil drives the device-flow poll loop end-to-end. Most embedders
428	// want this helper rather than calling PollDeviceAuth manually — it
429	// owns the loop discipline that RFC 8628 §5.5 calls out as the
430	// difference between a polite client and a DoS source.
431	//
432	// Behaviour:
433	//
434	//   - Waits dc.Interval (defaulting to 5s, clamped to 1s minimum)
435	//     between successive poll calls.
436	//   - On ErrSlowDown, bumps the interval by 5s permanently per RFC
437	//     8628 §3.5. Subsequent slow_down responses bump again.
438	//   - Stops with the most-recent error when dc.ExpiresIn elapses since
439	//     PollUntil was called. If the AS omitted expires_in (zero or
440	//     negative), falls back to defaultExpiresIn so the loop is always
441	//     bounded — closes a hostile-AS DoS vector parallel to the
442	//     pollInterval clamp.
443	//   - Returns the TokenSet on success.
444	//   - Returns ctx.Err() (wrapped) when the caller cancels.
445	//   - Returns terminal sentinels (ErrAccessDenied, ErrExpiredToken,
446	//     ErrInvalidGrant) unwrapped, plus any unknown OAuth error verbatim,
447	//     so callers can errors.Is.
448	func (c *Client) PollUntil(ctx context.Context, dc *DeviceCode) (*tokens.TokenSet, error) {
449		if dc == nil {
450			return nil, errors.New("PollUntil: DeviceCode is nil")
451		}
452		if dc.DeviceCode == "" {
453			return nil, errors.New("PollUntil: DeviceCode.DeviceCode is empty")
454		}
455	
456		interval := pollInterval(dc)
457		expiresInSecs, defaulted := pollExpiresIn(dc)
458		deadline := nowFunc().Add(time.Duration(expiresInSecs) * time.Second)
459	
460		for {
461			ts, err := c.PollDeviceAuth(ctx, dc.DeviceCode)
462			switch {
463			case err == nil:
464				return ts, nil
465			case errors.Is(err, ErrAuthorizationPending):
466				// keep polling
467			case errors.Is(err, ErrSlowDown):
468				interval += slowDownBump
469			default:
470				// All other errors (terminal sentinels, unknown OAuth
471				// codes, network/decode failures) are propagated. The
472				// caller decides whether to retry.
473				return nil, err
474			}
475	
476			if !nowFunc().Before(deadline) {
477				if defaulted {
478					return nil, fmt.Errorf("PollUntil: default expiry (%ds) reached; AS omitted expires_in", expiresInSecs)
479				}
480				return nil, fmt.Errorf("PollUntil: device code expired after %ds", expiresInSecs)
481			}
482	
483			select {
484			case <-ctx.Done():
485				return nil, fmt.Errorf("PollUntil: %w", ctx.Err())
486			case <-time.After(interval):
487			}
488		}
489	}
490	
491	// defaultPollExpiresIn caps PollUntil when the AS omits expires_in.
492	// 30 minutes mirrors what most production device-flow servers issue
493	// (RFC 8628 doesn't mandate a value); long enough that legitimate
494	// users have time to authenticate, short enough that a buggy server
495	// can't keep us polling indefinitely. Declared as a var so the
496	// PollUntil tests can shrink it without burning real wall-clock
497	// minutes; production code must not mutate it.
498	var defaultPollExpiresIn = 30 * 60
499	
500	// pollExpiresIn returns the effective expires_in (in seconds) for a
501	// device-code response, plus whether the value came from the default
502	// fallback (true) or the wire value (false). RFC 8628 expects the AS
503	// to provide expires_in, but a buggy or hostile server might omit
504	// it — in which case we must still bound the loop.
505	func pollExpiresIn(dc *DeviceCode) (secs int, defaulted bool) {
506		if dc.ExpiresIn <= 0 {
507			return defaultPollExpiresIn, true
508		}
509		return dc.ExpiresIn, false
510	}

1	// Package tokens defines the post-protocol token shape and helpers for
2	// reading unverified claims out of JWT access tokens.
3	//
4	// The wire-shape responses from RFC 8628 / RFC 8693 endpoints are
5	// translated into a single TokenSet with absolute expiry. Clients that
6	// only ever see access tokens as opaque bearer strings need not import
7	// this package directly.
8	package tokens
9	
10	import (
11		"encoding/base64"
12		"encoding/json"
13		"errors"
14		"fmt"
15		"strings"
16		"time"
17	)
18	
19	// TokenSet is an OAuth token bundle returned from a device-flow or
20	// token-exchange endpoint, normalised to absolute expiry.
21	//
22	// RefreshToken is empty when the issuer didn't return one. ExpiresAt is
23	// zero for tokens that don't carry a wire-side expires_in.
24	type TokenSet struct {
25		AccessToken  string
26		RefreshToken string
27		TokenType    string
28		ExpiresAt    time.Time
29		Scope        string
30	}
31	
32	// HasRefresh reports whether the set carries a refresh token.
33	func (t TokenSet) HasRefresh() bool { return t.RefreshToken != "" }
34	
35	// Expired reports whether the access token's advertised lifetime has
36	// elapsed at now. Returns false for tokens with a zero ExpiresAt.
37	func (t TokenSet) Expired(now time.Time) bool {
38		if t.ExpiresAt.IsZero() {
39			return false
40		}
41		return !now.Before(t.ExpiresAt)
42	}
43	
44	// ShouldRefresh reports whether the access token is within skew of
45	// expiring (or has already expired). Tokens without an advertised
46	// expiry never need refreshing.
47	func (t TokenSet) ShouldRefresh(now time.Time, skew time.Duration) bool {
48		if t.ExpiresAt.IsZero() {
49			return false
50		}
51		return !now.Add(skew).Before(t.ExpiresAt)
52	}
53	
54	// Claims holds the fields parsed from a JWT access token's payload.
55	//
56	// Signature verification is the issuing server's responsibility; this
57	// package never validates signatures. Clients read claims for routing
58	// (which issuer, which audience) and UX (display the principal handle).
59	type Claims struct {
60		Issuer    string
61		Subject   string
62		Audience  []string
63		Handle    string
64		ExpiresAt time.Time
65		IssuedAt  time.Time
66		NotBefore time.Time
67	}
68	
69	// ErrMalformedJWT is returned by ParseClaims when the input is not a
70	// well-formed JWT (three base64url-encoded segments separated by dots).
71	var ErrMalformedJWT = errors.New("malformed JWT")
72	
73	// ErrUnsignedJWT is returned by ParseClaims when the JWT header
74	// declares `alg: none`. The unsigned-JWT shape was deprecated by
75	// RFC 7518 §3.6 and is a known attack vector (an attacker can craft
76	// arbitrary claims that pass shape checks). Defense in depth: even
77	// though this package never trusts claims for authorization
78	// decisions, we refuse to parse them so a future caller can't be
79	// tricked into routing on attacker-controlled values.
80	var ErrUnsignedJWT = errors.New("refusing to parse unsigned JWT (alg:none)")
81	
82	// ParseClaims decodes the payload segment of jwt without verifying the
83	// signature. Audience is normalised to a slice even when the wire form
84	// is a single string.
85	//
86	// Rejects JWTs whose header declares `alg: none` — see ErrUnsignedJWT
87	// for the rationale. The signature payload itself is still not
88	// verified; that remains the issuing server's responsibility.
89	func ParseClaims(jwt string) (*Claims, error) {
90		parts := strings.Split(jwt, ".")
91		if len(parts) != 3 {
92			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: expected 3 segments, got %d", ErrMalformedJWT, len(parts))
93		}
94	
95		header, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[0])
96		if err != nil {
97			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode JWT header: %w", err)
98		}
99		var hdr struct {
100			Alg string `json:"alg"`
101		}
102		if err := json.Unmarshal(header, &hdr); err != nil {
103			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode JWT header: %w", err)
104		}
105		// JWS algorithm identifiers (RFC 7515 §4.1.1, IANA "JSON Web
106		// Signature and Encryption Algorithms" registry) are ASCII
107		// alphanumeric only — "HS256", "RS512", "EdDSA", "none", …
108		//
109		// Anything else is malformed. Rejecting non-alphanumeric runes
110		// here closes a class of bypasses against the alg:none check:
111		// `strings.TrimSpace` only handles unicode.IsSpace, missing
112		// U+200B (zero-width space), U+FEFF (BOM), and other invisible
113		// chars that a hostile AS could pad around "none" to slip past
114		// a case-fold comparison.
115		for _, r := range hdr.Alg {
116			if (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9') {
117				continue
118			}
119			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: alg contains non-alphanumeric character", ErrMalformedJWT)
120		}
121		// Case-insensitive because RFC 7515 §4.1.1 doesn't strictly
122		// canonicalise case, and "None" / "NONE" have been observed in
123		// the wild.
124		if strings.EqualFold(hdr.Alg, "none") {
125			return nil, ErrUnsignedJWT
126		}
127	
128		payload, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[1])
129		if err != nil {
130			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode JWT payload: %w", err)
131		}
132	
133		var raw struct {
134			Iss    string          `json:"iss"`
135			Sub    string          `json:"sub"`
136			Aud    json.RawMessage `json:"aud"`
137			Exp    int64           `json:"exp"`
138			Iat    int64           `json:"iat"`
139			Nbf    int64           `json:"nbf"`
140			Handle string          `json:"handle"`
141		}
142		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &raw); err != nil {
143			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode JWT claims: %w", err)
144		}
145	
146		c := &Claims{
147			Issuer:  raw.Iss,
148			Subject: raw.Sub,
149			Handle:  raw.Handle,
150		}
151	
152		if raw.Exp != 0 {
153			c.ExpiresAt = time.Unix(raw.Exp, 0).UTC()
154		}
155		if raw.Iat != 0 {
156			c.IssuedAt = time.Unix(raw.Iat, 0).UTC()
157		}
158		if raw.Nbf != 0 {
159			c.NotBefore = time.Unix(raw.Nbf, 0).UTC()
160		}
161	
162		c.Audience, err = decodeAudience(raw.Aud)
163		if err != nil {
164			return nil, err
165		}
166	
167		return c, nil
168	}
169	
170	// decodeAudience handles both string and string-array forms of the JWT
171	// `aud` claim.
172	func decodeAudience(raw json.RawMessage) ([]string, error) {
173		if len(raw) == 0 {
174			return nil, nil
175		}
176	
177		var single string
178		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &single); err == nil {
179			if single == "" {
180				return nil, nil
181			}
182			return []string{single}, nil
183		}
184	
185		var multi []string
186		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &multi); err == nil {
187			return multi, nil
188		}
189	
190		return nil, errors.New("decode JWT aud claim: not a string or array")
191	}

2	// the Keyring reference implementation.
3	//
4	// Profile is whatever string the caller wants to key by — typically a
5	// base URL, a kubectl-style context name, or a principal handle.
6	package tokenstore
7	
8	import (
9		"errors"

11		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokens"

19	// can't be decoded into a TokenSet. Used by callers that want to treat
20	// a malformed entry as a legacy/upgrade path (e.g. pre-shim bare-string
21	// entries from older binaries) without confusing it with transport
22	// errors from the underlying keyring.

25	// Store persists token bundles keyed by an opaque profile string.
26	//
27	// Implementations must:
28	//   - Return ErrNotFound (not a zero value, no error) when LoadTokens
29	//     is called for an unknown profile.
30	//   - Treat DeleteTokens of a missing profile as a no-op.
31	//   - Not write empty access tokens; SaveTokens should reject them.
32	type Store interface {
33		SaveTokens(profile string, t tokens.TokenSet) error
34		LoadTokens(profile string) (tokens.TokenSet, error)
35		DeleteTokens(profile string) error
36	}

1	// Package sts is an RFC 8693 OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange client.
2	//
3	// Construct a Client with the issuer's BaseURL and the token endpoint
4	// path, then call Exchange with a populated ExchangeRequest. The
5	// package is provider-agnostic: every server-specific value (endpoint
6	// path, requested-token-type URIs, custom form fields) is supplied at
7	// call time. There is no provider detection.
8	package sts
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"errors"
13		"fmt"
14		"net/http"
15		"net/url"
16		"strings"
17		"time"
18	
19		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/internal/oauthhttp"
20		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokens"
21	)
22	
23	// nowFunc is the package's clock. Override in tests.
24	var nowFunc = time.Now
25	
26	// RFC 8693 grant_type and standard subject-token type URIs. Caller
27	// supplies RequestedTokenType (which is always implementation-specific
28	// outside of these RFC 8693 standard values).
29	const (
30		GrantTypeTokenExchange = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange" //nolint:gosec // RFC 8693 grant_type URI, not a credential
31	
32		SubjectTokenTypeJWT         = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt"          //nolint:gosec // RFC 8693 token-type URI, not a credential
33		SubjectTokenTypeAccessToken = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token" //nolint:gosec // RFC 8693 token-type URI, not a credential
34	)
35	
36	// ExchangeRequest is the input to a token exchange.
37	//
38	// SubjectToken, SubjectTokenType, and RequestedTokenType are required.
39	// Audience, Resource, and Scope map to RFC 8693 §2.1 parameters and
40	// are sent only when non-empty. Extra carries implementation-specific
41	// form fields (e.g. server-defined parameters not in RFC 8693) that
42	// the caller's server expects; the standard fields above always win
43	// if Extra also sets them.
44	type ExchangeRequest struct {
45		SubjectToken       string
46		SubjectTokenType   string
47		RequestedTokenType string
48	
49		Audience string
50		Resource string
51		Scope    string
52	
53		Extra url.Values
54	}
55	
56	func (r ExchangeRequest) validate() error {
57		switch {
58		case r.SubjectToken == "":
59			return errors.New("SubjectToken is required")
60		case r.SubjectTokenType == "":
61			return errors.New("SubjectTokenType is required")
62		case r.RequestedTokenType == "":
63			return errors.New("RequestedTokenType is required")
64		}
65		return nil
66	}
67	
68	// DefaultRequestTimeout caps a single token-exchange round-trip. Set
69	// conservatively: even with a slow auth host plus TLS handshake, a
70	// healthy exchange completes in sub-seconds. The cap mainly defends
71	// against slow-loris responses dripping bytes within MaxResponseBytes
72	// — see Client.RequestTimeout for the per-Client override.
73	const DefaultRequestTimeout = 30 * time.Second
74	
75	// Client exchanges subject tokens for tokens of a different type at an
76	// RFC 8693 token endpoint.
77	//
78	// All configuration is explicit; the package has no global state and
79	// no implicit URLs. Provide BaseURL and Path; the rest is RFC 8693.
80	type Client struct {
81		// Transport supplies the http.RoundTripper used for all calls.
82		// nil → http.DefaultTransport. The library builds its own
83		// *http.Client around this transport so callers can't trivially
84		// pass a *http.Client with TLS verification disabled. See the
85		// deviceflow.Client.Transport doc for the security rationale.
86		Transport http.RoundTripper
87	
88		BaseURL   string
89		Path      string
90		UserAgent string
91	
92		// RequestTimeout is the per-Exchange deadline applied via
93		// context.WithTimeout on top of the caller's context. Zero falls
94		// back to DefaultRequestTimeout. Negative disables the cap (useful
95		// for tests that want to drive timing via the caller's ctx alone).
96		RequestTimeout time.Duration
97	
98		// AllowInsecureHTTP permits http:// BaseURLs. Default (false) is
99		// reject — token exchanges carry the subject token (a bearer) on
100		// the wire and must be TLS-protected end to end. Production callers
101		// MUST leave this false; only tests and local development that pin
102		// the issuer to loopback should flip it.
103		AllowInsecureHTTP bool
104	}
105	
106	// Exchange performs one RFC 8693 token exchange.
107	//
108	// Returns a TokenSet with absolute ExpiresAt derived from the server's
109	// expires_in. Returns an error wrapping the response body when the
110	// server responds with a non-2xx status; callers can match on the
111	// returned error message for known OAuth error codes.
112	func (c *Client) Exchange(ctx context.Context, req ExchangeRequest) (*tokens.TokenSet, error) {
113		if err := req.validate(); err != nil {
114			return nil, fmt.Errorf("token exchange: %w", err)
115		}
116	
117		form := buildForm(req)
118	
119		endpoint, err := resolveURL(c.BaseURL, c.Path, c.AllowInsecureHTTP)
120		if err != nil {
121			return nil, fmt.Errorf("token exchange: resolve URL: %w", err)
122		}
123	
124		if timeout := c.requestTimeout(); timeout > 0 {
125			var cancel context.CancelFunc
126			ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
127			defer cancel()
128		}
129	
130		httpReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, endpoint, strings.NewReader(form.Encode()))
131		if err != nil {
132			return nil, fmt.Errorf("token exchange: create request: %w", err)
133		}
134		httpReq.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
135		httpReq.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
136		if c.UserAgent != "" {
137			httpReq.Header.Set("User-Agent", c.UserAgent)
138		}
139	
140		resp, err := c.httpClient().Do(httpReq)
141		if err != nil {
142			return nil, fmt.Errorf("token exchange: %w", err)
143		}
144		defer resp.Body.Close()
145	
146		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
147			return nil, readAPIError(resp)
148		}
149	
150		var raw struct {
151			AccessToken     string `json:"access_token"`
152			IssuedTokenType string `json:"issued_token_type"`
153			TokenType       string `json:"token_type"`
154			ExpiresIn       int    `json:"expires_in"`
155			RefreshToken    string `json:"refresh_token"`
156			Scope           string `json:"scope"`
157		}
158		if err := oauthhttp.ReadAndDecodeJSON(resp.Body, &raw, false); err != nil {
159			return nil, fmt.Errorf("token exchange: %w", err)
160		}
161		if raw.AccessToken == "" {
162			return nil, errors.New("token exchange: response missing access_token")
163		}
164	
165		// Exchanged tokens are short-lived per RFC 8693 §2.2.1's spirit
166		// (the whole point of exchange is to issue narrowly-scoped,
167		// short-lived bearers). A missing or non-positive expires_in is
168		// either misconfiguration or a hostile AS — either way, we refuse
169		// to cache a token of unknown lifetime and force a fresh exchange.
170		if raw.ExpiresIn <= 0 {
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("token exchange: non-positive expires_in (%d)", raw.ExpiresIn)
172		}
173	
174		return &tokens.TokenSet{
175			AccessToken:  raw.AccessToken,
176			RefreshToken: raw.RefreshToken,
177			TokenType:    raw.TokenType,
178			Scope:        raw.Scope,
179			ExpiresAt:    nowFunc().Add(time.Duration(raw.ExpiresIn) * time.Second),
180		}, nil
181	}
182	
183	// buildForm renders an ExchangeRequest into the wire form, layering
184	// the standard RFC 8693 fields on top of req.Extra so caller-supplied
185	// duplicates of standard fields are overwritten by the typed values.
186	func buildForm(req ExchangeRequest) url.Values {
187		form := url.Values{}
188		for k, v := range req.Extra {
189			form[k] = append(form[k], v...)
190		}
191	
192		form.Set("grant_type", GrantTypeTokenExchange)
193		form.Set("subject_token", req.SubjectToken)
194		form.Set("subject_token_type", req.SubjectTokenType)
195		form.Set("requested_token_type", req.RequestedTokenType)
196	
197		if req.Audience != "" {
198			form.Set("audience", req.Audience)
199		}
200		if req.Resource != "" {
201			form.Set("resource", req.Resource)
202		}
203		if req.Scope != "" {
204			form.Set("scope", req.Scope)
205		}
206		return form
207	}
208	
209	// httpClient builds the *http.Client used for one Exchange call. See
210	// oauthhttp.HTTPClient for the construction policy.
211	func (c *Client) httpClient() *http.Client {
212		return oauthhttp.HTTPClient(c.Transport)
213	}
214	
215	// requestTimeout resolves the effective per-request timeout: the
216	// configured RequestTimeout if positive, the package default if zero,
217	// or zero (no cap) if negative.
218	func (c *Client) requestTimeout() time.Duration {
219		switch {
220		case c.RequestTimeout < 0:
221			return 0
222		case c.RequestTimeout == 0:
223			return DefaultRequestTimeout
224		default:
225			return c.RequestTimeout
226		}
227	}
228	
229	// ErrInsecureBaseURL is returned when Exchange is called against an
230	// http:// BaseURL without AllowInsecureHTTP set. Token exchange ships
231	// a subject_token (typically the user's core bearer) in the request
232	// body — over plain HTTP that's a credential in the clear. Re-exported
233	// from internal/oauthhttp so callers can errors.Is uniformly across
234	// deviceflow and sts.
235	var ErrInsecureBaseURL = oauthhttp.ErrInsecureBaseURL
236	
237	// ErrAbsolutePath is returned when Path is an absolute or
238	// scheme-relative URL rather than a path relative to BaseURL. See
239	// oauthhttp.ErrAbsolutePath for the rationale; re-exported here so
240	// callers can errors.Is on either package's sentinel.
241	var ErrAbsolutePath = oauthhttp.ErrAbsolutePath
242	
243	func resolveURL(baseURL, path string, allowInsecureHTTP bool) (string, error) {
244		return oauthhttp.ResolveURL(baseURL, path, allowInsecureHTTP) //nolint:wrapcheck // pass through with sentinel-preserving semantics
245	}
246	
247	func readAPIError(resp *http.Response) error {
248		apiErr, parseErr := oauthhttp.ReadOAuthError(resp)
249		if parseErr != nil {
250			return fmt.Errorf("token exchange: %w", parseErr)
251		}
252		if desc := oauthhttp.SanitizeDescription(apiErr.ErrorDescription); desc != "" {
253			return fmt.Errorf("token exchange: status %d: %s: %s", resp.StatusCode, apiErr.Error, desc)
254		}
255		return fmt.Errorf("token exchange: status %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, apiErr.Error)
256	}

+// NewAuthenticatedAPIClient creates an API client targeting api.BaseURL()

All tasks complete. Here's a summary of what shipped on `soph/auth-go`:

## Summary

**24 files changed: +678 / -260**

### New files
- `cmd/entire/cli/auth/provider.go` — `Provider` table (v1 single-host, v2 split-host with STSPath `/api/authz/sts/token`), `CurrentProvider()`, `SetProviderForTest()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/auth/exchange.go` — `TokenForResource(ctx, url)` / `Token(ctx, req)` shims over `tokenmanager.Manager`, with lazy singleton + loopback-HTTP auto-permit
- `cmd/entire/cli/auth/provider_test.go`, `login_validate_test.go` — new unit coverage

### Key migrations
- **Library wired in**: `go.mod` pinned to `github.com/entireio/auth-go v0.1.1-0.20260520123811-da94c52ef430` (PR #5 head, with the hardened OAuth checks). Go bumped 1.26.2 → 1.26.3 per the lib's `go.mod`.
- **`auth/client.go`**: now a thin shim over `deviceflow.Client`, using `Transport` (not `HTTP`) per PR #5. Surfaces unknown OAuth codes through `DeviceAuthPoll.Error/ErrorDescription` so login fails fast on terminal rejections.
- **`auth/store.go`**: implements `tokenstore.Store`. JSON-shape rejection on read so corrupt entries don't end up as `Bearer …`. Keys tokens by `AuthBaseURL()`.
- **Split-host config**: `api.AuthBaseURL()` falls back to `BaseURL()` (single-host unchanged). `requireSecureBaseURL` now checks both origins.
- **`api.Client`**: new `NewClientWithBaseURL` + `WithAuthTokensPath` so auth-token endpoints route through the provider table. `bearerTransport` refuses empty bearers up-front.
- **Data-API callers**: `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient(ctx, …)` now goes through `auth.TokenForResource(ctx, api.BaseURL())`, threading ctx through activity, dispatch_wizard, recap, search, trail, watch.
- **`dispatch/mode_cloud.go`**: routes through `lookupResourceToken` so split-host gets the RFC 8693 exchanged bearer.
- **`search_cmd.go`**: drops path/query from `ENTIRE_SEARCH_URL` before passing to TokenForResource (the new origin-URL validation from auth-go PR #5 would otherwise reject it). Defaults `serviceURL` to `api.BaseURL()` instead of `search.DefaultServiceURL`.
- **`login.go`**: `validateReceivedToken` parses claims, rejects `alg:none` via `tokens.ErrUnsignedJWT`, checks `iss` and pre-expired `exp` before persisting.

### Verification
- `go build ./...` clean
- `mise run test` — 5294 tests pass, 3 skipped
- `mise run test:integration` — 348 tests pass
- `mise run lint` — 0 Go issues (only flag is `lint:gomod` complaining `go.mod`/`go.sum` are uncommitted, which is expected — these are part of the change)

Branch is ready for review; nothing committed since you didn't ask for that.

# Simplify: Code Review and Cleanup

Review all changed files for reuse, quality, and efficiency. Fix any issues found.

## Phase 1: Identify Changes

Run `git diff` (or `git diff HEAD` if there are staged changes) to see what changed. If there are no git changes, review the most recently modified files that the user mentioned or that you edited earlier in this conversation.

## Phase 2: Launch Three Review Agents in Parallel

Use the Agent tool to launch all three agents concurrently in a single message. Pass each agent the full diff so it has the complete context.

### Agent 1: Code Reuse Review

For each change:

1. **Search for existing utilities and helpers** that could replace newly written code. Look for similar patterns elsewhere in the codebase — common locations are utility directories, shared modules, and files adjacent to the changed ones.
2. **Flag any new function that duplicates existing functionality.** Suggest the existing function to use instead.
3. **Flag any inline logic that could use an existing utility** — hand-rolled string manipulation, manual path handling, custom environment checks, ad-hoc type guards, and similar patterns are common candidates.

### Agent 2: Code Quality Review

Review the same changes for hacky patterns:

1. **Redundant state**: state that duplicates existing state, cached values that could be derived, observers/effects that could be direct calls
2. **Parameter sprawl**: adding new parameters to a function instead of generalizing or restructuring existing ones
3. **Copy-paste with slight variation**: near-duplicate code blocks that should be unified with a shared abstraction
4. **Leaky abstractions**: exposing internal details that should be encapsulated, or breaking existing abstraction boundaries
5. **Stringly-typed code**: using raw strings where constants, enums (string unions), or branded types already exist in the codebase
6. **Unnecessary JSX nesting**: wrapper Boxes/elements that add no layout value — check if inner component props (flexShrink, alignItems, etc.) already provide the needed behavior
7. **Nested conditionals**: ternary chains (`a ? x : b ? y : ...`), nested if/else, or nested switch 3+ levels deep — flatten with early returns, guard clauses, a lookup table, or an if/else-if cascade
8. **Unnecessary comments**: comments explaining WHAT the code does (well-named identifiers already do that), narrating the change, or referencing the task/caller — delete; keep only non-obvious WHY (hidden constraints, subtle invariants, workarounds)

### Agent 3: Efficiency Review

Review the same changes for efficiency:

1. **Unnecessary work**: redundant computations, repeated file reads, duplicate network/API calls, N+1 patterns
2. **Missed concurrency**: independent operations run sequentially when they could run in parallel
3. **Hot-path bloat**: new blocking work added to startup or per-request/per-render hot paths
4. **Recurring no-op updates**: state/store updates inside polling loops, intervals, or event handlers that fire unconditionally — add a change-detection guard so downstream consumers aren't notified when nothing changed. Also: if a wrapper function takes an updater/reducer callback, verify it honors same-reference returns (or whatever the "no change" signal is) — otherwise callers' early-return no-ops are silently defeated
5. **Unnecessary existence checks**: pre-checking file/resource existence before operating (TOCTOU anti-pattern) — operate directly and handle the error
6. **Memory**: unbounded data structures, missing cleanup, event listener leaks
7. **Overly broad operations**: reading entire files when only a portion is needed, loading all items when filtering for one

## Phase 3: Fix Issues

Wait for all three agents to complete. Aggregate their findings and fix each issue directly. If a finding is a false positive or not worth addressing, note it and move on — do not argue with the finding, just skip it.

When done, briefly summarize what was fixed (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.text:
All 5294 tests still pass.

## Simplify Summary

Aggregated findings from 3 parallel agents; applied 5 high-value fixes:

1. **Race-safe `managerForTest`** (`auth/exchange.go`) — added `managerTestMu` to match `provider.go`'s pattern. The previous unguarded access was a data race waiting to happen if any future test uses `SetManagerForTest` under `t.Parallel()`.

2. **Extracted `api.OriginOnly(string) string`** — single helper replaces `searchTokenResourceURL` in `search_cmd.go` and the body of `normalizeIssuer`/`issMatches` in `login.go`. Both were doing identical "parse URL, keep scheme+host, fall through on parse failure" logic. Deleted 30+ lines of duplicate code.

3. **`newAuthHostAPIClient(token)` helper** in `auth.go` — replaces three copy-paste sites (`defaultListTokens`, `defaultRevokeTokenByID`, `defaultRevokeCurrentToken`) that each wrote `api.NewClientWithBaseURL(token, api.AuthBaseURL()).WithAuthTokensPath(auth.CurrentProvider().AuthTokensPath)`.

4. **Skip redundant URL parse in single-host mode** — `requireSecureBaseURL` (`auth.go`) and `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient` (`api_client.go`) now short-circuit the second `RequireSecureURL` when `AuthBaseURL() == BaseURL()`, which is the common case.

5. **Reuse `dataURL` local in `api_client.go`** — `TokenForResource` now uses the already-resolved `dataURL` instead of re-calling `api.BaseURL()`.

Skipped (low value or by design):
- Micro-optimizing `looksJSONShaped` (keyring I/O dominates the per-call cost by ~6 orders of magnitude)
- Memoizing `BaseURL`/`AuthBaseURL` (adds sync.Once complexity for an env-read + 2x `strings.Trim`)
- Removing deprecated `SaveToken`/`GetToken`/`DeleteToken` (explicitly retained as the migration bridge per their doc comments)
- Unifying the dispatch test stub helpers (different test scenarios genuinely need different swap shapes; the duplication is shallow)
- Dropping one-liner godocs on shim methods (standard Go practice for exported symbols)

Verification: build clean, `mise run fmt && mise run lint` → 0 issues, full test run → 5294 tests pass.
